old: The coordination multiplier uses the paper’s exponent 1.227, comparing communities of 500 with 100 people. Treating this association as a causal productivity gain is an explicit experimental assumption.
new: The published exponent 1.227 is a size association between communities of 500 and 100 people. It is not a measured productivity effect. The default coordination multiplier is 1, so the association has no causal effect unless the multiplier is raised. The old base-5 value 5^0.227 (about 1.44) and a midpoint (about 1.20) are sensitivities.
why: 5.1: 5^0.227 has an arbitrary base of 5 and the 1.227 exponent is a size association, not a causal productivity effect. Default multiplier is now 1; the old value and a midpoint are sensitivities. Relocation exit and Petri recovery depend on this (see README).
